# Relightable 3D Gaussian
Also called: Relightable 3D Gaussian Splatting
## Overview
Relightable 3D Gaussian extends 3D Gaussian [Splatting](#23-splatting.md) by assigning per-Gaussian [BRDF](#14809-bidirectional-reflectance-distribution-function-brdf.md) parameters and precomputed visibility to enable dynamic relighting and shadow casting [S1, unofficial]. It distinguishes itself from standard 3D Gaussian Splatting by evaluating material responses to arbitrary light sources rather than relying solely on captured environment maps [S1, unofficial]. Builds on [BRDF and Relighting Extensions](6227-brdf-and-relighting-extensions.md).
## How it works
**Inputs:** A set of 3D Gaussians $\{G_i\}$ storing per-Gaussian BRDF parameters (albedo, roughness, normal) and precomputed visibility for shadows [S1, unofficial]. Scene lighting configuration (direction, intensity, type) [G].
**Outputs:** A rendered image with physically plausible shading, including shadows and specular reflections based on the defined BRDF [G].
**Data Structures:** Each Gaussian $i$ stores: albedo $\rho_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$ (diffuse color), roughness $r_i \in \mathbb{R}$ (microfacet roughness), normal $n_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$ (surface orientation), and visibility $v_i$ (shadow occlusion factor) [S1, unofficial].
**Steps:** Not given in the sources.

## Subtopics

### R3DG
R3DG is a variant that combines BRDF parameters with ambient-occlusion baked per Gaussian [S1, unofficial]. When to choose it or its link is not given in the sources [S1, unofficial].

## Operating characteristics
Time and memory complexity, measured performance, scaling, strengths, limitations, and usage guidelines are not given in the sources [S1, unofficial].
## Background
Relightable 3D Gaussian was introduced by [Gao et al](#9230-n-dimensional-gaussian-6dgs-7dgs.md). in ECCV'24 [S1, unofficial]. It addresses the limitation of standard 3D Gaussian Splatting in handling dynamic lighting and physically based materials [S1, unofficial].
